Niesamowity pomysł na poprowadzenie fabuły – można poczuć się jak prawdziwy operator siedzący na linii z agentami i wspomagający ich w analizowaniu informacji. W fabule wplecione są smaczki z używaniem terminala, przepisywaniem informacji, rozgryzaniem kodów itd. Świetnie się bawiłem. The storyline is incredibly well-crafted – you can really feel like a true operator sitting on the line with agents and assisting them in analyzing information. The user interface and sound effects are brilliant – it's definitely worth wearing headphones. The plot is interwoven with elements like using terminals, transcribing information, decoding, etc. I had a great time. The only downside is that the adventure is short, but on the other hand, the tension is maintained throughout. I don't regret a single second spent at the keyboard. Superb narration. Congratulations to the creators.

This isn't right, I should be giving this game a positive review. This game caught me fresh out of watching an episode of Monk, so I was up for a good detective game and for the most part, it delivered. The investigating, the story, the puzzles to solve, all solid and well designed.

But that ending... &$!" THAT ENDING! Without spoiling too much, no matter what you do, whether you succeed or fail certain tasks. It always ends the same. You die, the bad guys win and nearly everyone on your side is quietly eliminated. We then get a jump to the present day with a potential cliffhanger, but it comes off as nothing more than sequel bait. I mean, come on! At least in L.A.Noire, you still foiled the conspirators' scheme. This is just a huge middle finger to the player.

Needless to say, I did some digging. This couldn't be how the game actually ends right? There has to be a good ending you need to meet a certain requirement for.
Turns out I'm not the only one doing this, but all the players have dug up is a hidden message that comes up if you enter a password into a file before you're supposed to know it.
It doesn't really explain anything.

What an utter cop out. Hey is any gaming channel working on a Top 10 worst video game endings? I think we've found a good contender.

(Edit: That jester award is probably from that guy in the forums who's going around harassing anyone who shares my opinion. Guy just can't take the idea that people see this game's ending as awful.)

I'm pretty conflicted regarding my thoughts on this game, if there was a neutral review that would be my rating. 

On one hand the game is very polished, especially for an indie game. It's OST really sets the mood and switches at the perfect time to give you goosebumps. The mechanics are pretty fleshed out; providing a decent challenge while also not being so hard that would require one to search up guides on them. The story is also really thought out and you will get invested into it very quick.

The unfortunate problem I have with this game is that it's extremely short. You can tell by the average 3 hour playtime in the reviews. Additionally all the content + mechanics that the game will throw at your are pretty much in the trailer. (There's only like 10 cases in total) Additionally, all game choices seems to not divert things from the main ending, which means that the game is not very re-playable. There may be some secrets as hinted by the credits achievement or that can be activated by a certain specific sequence of events, but they aren't readily accessible and would require probably some video tutorial guide.

And that leads to the big question, should you buy the game? I honestly can't say in good faith that it is worth it to buy the listed price ($14 USD). If you have a good amount of spare money to spend on games, then go for it. But for most people, I'd recommend holding out on purchasing the game unless it has a heavy sale.

This is a very short game, you'll be done in 3 hours if you're competent at basic puzzles ~ less if you spam the hint feature.

This is an investigation game, where you're an operator in the FDI (or FBI really), and the investigative features boil down to clicking on images and connecting evidence when asked to do so. There's the odd puzzle, but it isn't particularly difficult ~ the hardest part is a timed segment, which you can get around by pausing the game, as all the information remains on screen anyway.

Really, you're here to play this for the storyline, which is a fairly predictable conspiracy laced, X-files, deep-state mystery. The twists are fairly obvious, but the execution of the story beats/elements are lacking. 

It feels as if the story would have better served from being a bit longer, given more time to stew a bit. There's unnecessary padding, in full blur cut scenes that take place between each 'day', and they seem to exist either for 'atmosphere' or more cynically, just to pad the game out so you go over the 2 hour refund mark. (Your mileage may vary, they did nothing for me but waste time.)

For £10, it is... okay? At best. There's one ending, as far as I know, so there's little reason to replay the game. As a one-shot experience, it is decent, but I think it is better on a deeper sale, something around £5-7 maybe, as this is such a niche experience, it doesn't really do anything new.

If you're an X-Files fans, or someone who loves conspiracy theories, lizard people behind the scenes (or a flat-Earther, whatever), you'll be right at home here. Otherwise, it is a fairly basic investigative game that doesn't quite nail the key plot points to take it beyond being simply decent.

It's an ok game to kill a couple hours. I'm recommending, because I love that people make these kind of games, but I am a bit disappointed. It's VERY easy. The demo gave me Vigil Cases vibe, but turned out the game has incredibly strong and inescapable hand-holding. It's like Vigil Cases in tutorial mode. I thought I'd be looking through a bunch of databases and burrowing into various documents to find details that would solve cases. In reality I was mostly clicking on the dialogue, where NPCs would tell me exactly what to do, which usually involved no more than opening one file, looking up one name, or following a list of instructions.

There was a lot of lost potential here. Like, there's literally zero point in the terminal: the player never gets to figure out what command they should enter, it's always provided by the NPCs. There's no choice who to call, or what information to tell them, except in a couple places. I counted two cool puzzles that gave you an "Aha" moment, the rest was unfortunately easy and predictable.

In short, if you're looking for something to scratch the 'Golden Idol" or "Roottrees are Dead" itch, I wouldn't get your hopes up.

Easily one of the most engaging and immersive detective games that I just couldn't help but finish in one sitting. And what a beautiful soundtrack. Support indie gems like this - totally worth it at full price and more.

kinda wish i could leave a "mixed" review because i don't hate this game - it does a lot of cool and interesting things and scratches a little bit at an itch left by hypnospace outlaw and home safety hotline, however the game is extremely short (a casual run through is about 3 hours, i can imagine someone who understands and quickly solves all the puzzles immediately on their first playthrough could potentially complete it in half that time,) the game introduces multiple puzzle mechanics that it uses exactly once and never returns to, and it has zero replayability - there is only one ending, the nature of which i imagine many will find unsatisfying due to the negative outcome for the player character and his allies. this is in spite of the player SEEMINGLY having some control over the events that take place, but ultimately have no impact on the end of the game. the feeling i got by the end of the post-credits sequence was that i had just paid 16 bucks for just the prologue to the "real game" which doesn't exist.

speaking of prologues, if you played the demo and were drawn to the game due to the extraterrestrial / ufo themes that dominate that portion of the game, you'll be disappointed to know that this entire element is dropped immediately after the portion of the game covered by the demo ends, and never comes back. i'm not going to call this intentionally misleading, but i imagine a non-zero number of people who bought the game will walk away disappointed due to this fact.

finally, the game is a bit buggy and softlocks in multiple places - i recommend you follow what the game expects you to do in the exact order it likes, as getting ahead of yourself, either through experimentation or actual foreknowledge, can potentially end your entire run and you'll have to start over.

Think of a AAA game with only the first level.  Clearly the quality is top-notch but it's a bit baffling someone would put so much work into something so short.  This makes it almost feel like a long demo.

I really liked most of the game, and there is a level of attention to detail and craftsmanship present that all but the best indy titles usually lack. If there was more story so that the game ran 10-20 hours, it would be an easy 9/10, $40+, best game I've played this year. In it's current state, however, I feel like its worth about $10.

So, given its currently priced at $14, what's my final conclusion?  Tepid recommend.  I loved every minute, but given that there were so few of them, I feel a bit conflicted given the price.

I just really hope to see more in the future from this developer.  Make an Operator 2 with at least 10 hours of runtime, price it at ~$30 and you'll have me banging down your door to play.

Also, for those wondering, the game plays like a linear narrative adventure.  Your choices don't matter, but there is some light puzzling and detective work to keep you engaged. The game seems heavily inspired by Hacknet and Orwell, which is a great thing in my book.

Edit: Oh yes, I should mention it runs flawlessly on Windows 7

(This review contains information that might be considered spoilers for some, so read with caution!)

TL; DR:
It holds your hand throughout the game. The investigative puzzles are immersive, but simple and provides very little challenge. It's short, but you might possible still like it for it's presentation and story. If there was a "lukewarm" rating, I would pick that. But since it's clearly a labor of love, I'm inclined to rate positively.

The longer review:

When I heard of The Operator a few days before launch, I was hoping for something to scratch that Obra Dinn / Curse of the Golden Idol itch. Not very many games manage to make you feel like a proper investigator or makes you feel super clever when you progress, and those two games are the gold standard.

The Operator - unfortunately - is not that game.

The immersion is great. You definitely feel like an operator, scanning photos for details that you then input into various databases to yield result. The interface is exactly how you'd imagine a 90's 'hacker' terminal to look like, complete with a terminal and an official looking 'FBI' interface. The majority of the game is fully voiced with competent actors (for the budget).

Although a very polished and - for its medium - a cinematic experience, gameplay-wise it falls into many of the same pitfalls as other "investigative" games like it. The puzzles are - for the most part, but with notable exceptions - simple, requiring few steps to solve. Your hand is woefully held through each of them and the freedom to make your own deductions are sorely lacking. For the most part the tools required to solve a certain puzzle will appear when needed, and disappear when not needed anymore.

The story is decent and very on-par for such a game. It doesn't fully manage to suck you into the world, however. For one, the main plot felt rushed. You're a new operator working cases, and the very first case you receive is a part of a brewing conspiracy. Every case following that is connected in some way. In my opinion, the game doesn't take it's time to build up the world or the characters before placing you front and center into the main plot thread. 

Some of the major plot twists are extremely predictable, and some of what is presented as a major plot development honestly really isn't. We don't know the involved characters enough to care when the revelation is given to us.
The game also makes the cardinal sin of ending abruptly with no real resolution, most questions left unanswered and a feeling that your actions throughout the game had little impact.

A lot of this comes down to personal tastes, hopes and expectations, however. Chances are you'll like this game for it's good presentation and decent enough puzzles. It's not particularly expensive (though maybe a bit pricey for the estimated game time).
